A holiday plan for Lumi — two dates, two prices, your choice

Egypt in Spring

One week based in Cairo — the Pyramids, the brand-new Grand Egyptian Museum, old Islamic Cairo and evenings on the Nile — with the option to swap three nights for a cruise from Aswan to Luxor. Both good windows are priced side by side below so you can decide: mid-March for the best weather, or mid-April for a lower bill.

Option 1 · March: Sat 13 – Sat 20 Mar 2027 · Cairo ~24°C · Luxor ~30°C Option 2 · April: Sat 10 – Sat 17 Apr 2027 · Cairo ~28°C · Luxor ~35°C Flight: 4 hrs 50 mins direct from London Base: Cairo, with a Nile cruise option
March or April? The two plans & prices Flights Hotels Itinerary Nile cruise Budget Good to know

March or April? Both options, priced — you decide

No decision has been made for you. Both spring windows work, and the trade-off is simple: March buys you the best weather, April buys you a lower price — especially if you want the cruise. Here they are side by side, with the same two itineraries costed for each month. Pick the balance of heat vs. saving that suits you.

OPTION 1 · BEST WEATHER

Mid-March — Sat 13 to Sat 20 March 2027

Cairo ≈ 24°C by day, Luxor & Aswan ≈ 29–30°C. Full temple days are comfortable, evenings are cool, khamsin dust is less frequent. Just after Eid al-Fitr (expected ~9 March), and the week ends the day before cruise Easter peak pricing starts on 21 March.

Plan A · Cairo only: ≈ £900–£1,200 pp

Plan B · + Nile cruise: ≈ £1,580–£2,100 pp

You pay more for the cruise in March — it's high season on the river — but sightseeing is at its easiest.

OPTION 2 · BEST PRICE

Mid-April — Sat 10 to Sat 17 April 2027

Cairo ≈ 28°C by day — still pleasant — Luxor & Aswan ≈ 35°C, so temple visits need early starts and a midday break. Khamsin dust peaks in April. After Easter (28 March), so no Easter crowds or peak pricing.

Plan A · Cairo only: ≈ £880–£1,150 pp — saves ≈ £20–£50

Plan B · + Nile cruise: ≈ £1,480–£1,920 pp — saves ≈ £100–£180

The saving is real, and it's almost all on the cruise: April is shoulder season on the Nile, 15–20% cheaper for the same boat.

Mid-MarchMid-April
Cairo weather≈ 24°C by day, 13°C at night — ideal sightseeing≈ 28°C by day, 16°C at night — warm, still pleasant

So which would we pick? If the cruise is a must-have and budget matters most, April's saving is hard to ignore — you just plan around the southern heat. If comfort matters most, or you're staying in Cairo only (where the price gap is just £20–£50), March is the easier week. Either is a good trip — that's why both are left open for Lumi to choose.

And after April? Cheaper again — but too hot for a first trip

From May onwards prices fall further — cruises and hotels drop to low-season rates and you could save another £100–£250 per person on Plan B. The catch is the heat: by May Cairo is ≈ 32°C and Luxor & Aswan are 38–40°C+, rising through June. Temple sightseeing becomes a dawn-only activity with long, air-conditioned middays, and the river deck is too hot to enjoy. That's why this page stops at April: cheaper, yes — but for most people, too hot to get the best from the temples.

Sample weeks: 13–20 March sits just after Eid al-Fitr (expected ~9 March, moon-dependent) and before cruise Easter peak pricing from 21 March; 10–17 April sits after Easter Day (28 March), avoiding Easter peak. Temperatures are long-term climate averages (WMO normals). All prices per person, all-in estimates from the researched ranges below — see the two plans and the budget calculator, which now switches between March and April.

Two ways to spend the week — priced for both months

Two separate choices, both left to Lumi: which month (above) and which plan (here). Plan A — Cairo all week — is simpler and cheaper in either month. Plan B swaps three Cairo nights for the Nile, and sees far more of ancient Egypt, because the greatest temples aren't in Cairo at all — they're 650 km south, between Luxor and Aswan. All four combinations are priced:

Plan A

Cairo all week — 7 nights

Stay in one hotel, unpack once, and day-trip out: Giza and Saqqara, the Citadel and the bazaar, Coptic Cairo, and a day in Alexandria or the Fayoum oasis. Slow evenings, felucca rides, no internal flights.

March: ≈ £900–£1,200 per person

April: ≈ £880–£1,150 per person · saves ≈ £20–£50

Best if Lumi wants a relaxed pace and the lowest cost. Month makes little difference here — pick on weather.

Plan B

Cairo + Nile cruise — 4 + 3 nights

Four nights in Cairo for the Pyramids and museums, then fly south and sail Aswan → Luxor for three nights: Philae, Kom Ombo, Edfu, Karnak and the Valley of the Kings, with an Egyptologist on board.

March: ≈ £1,580–£2,100 per person

April: ≈ £1,480–£1,920 per person · saves ≈ £100–£180

The fuller first trip to Egypt — and the one where the month really changes the bill, because of cruise pricing.

Estimates built from the flight, hotel and cruise prices researched below (checked 20 November 2026, priced for both March and April 2027 travel). Use the budget calculator to mix and match month, flights, hotel and plan and see your own total.

Flights — London to Cairo

Direct flights leave London Heathrow daily with British Airways and EgyptAir and take just under five hours. In March Cairo is two hours ahead of London (the UK is still on GMT until 28 March); in April it's one hour ahead after UK clocks go forward. Fares are much the same in both months — March is historically one of the cheapest months on this route, April a touch higher outside Easter — so flights don't decide the month. Indirect flights via Istanbul, Athens or Vienna can be £80–£150 cheaper if the saving matters more than the time.

British Airways — flights to Egypt · Book the internal flights at the same time as the international ones if you can; through-tickets protect the connection.

Getting in from Cairo Airport

Cairo International (CAI) is about 45–60 minutes from Downtown and Zamalek depending on traffic — Cairo traffic is the one thing every visitor underestimates. Pre-book a hotel transfer or use Uber / Careem from the terminal; agree nothing with the touts inside arrivals. Expect roughly £8–£15 for the ride.

Visa — do it before you fly

UK and EU passport holders (including Romanian passports) can use Egypt's official e-Visa portal — visa2egypt.gov.eg — at US $30 for a single-entry tourist visa, applied for at least 7 days before departure, and print a copy. A visa on arrival at Cairo airport costs the same $30 in cash. Passport must be valid for at least six months from arrival.

Where to stay — reasonable, not rough

Three neighbourhoods, three different trips. Zamalek — a leafy island in the Nile — is the calmest and most walkable base, with cafés and restaurants on the doorstep. Downtown is louder and cheaper, steps from the old Egyptian Museum and the metro. Giza puts the Pyramids outside your window but leaves you far from everything else. For Lumi's first trip, Zamalek is the sweet spot.

TOP PICK · ZAMALEK

Longchamps Hotel

A long-running, family-feel boutique hotel at 21 Ismail Mohammed in the heart of Zamalek — quiet rooms, a pretty terrace, and the neighbourhood's restaurants a short stroll away. Rated 9.0–9.2 / 10 across 376–458 reviews.

March 2027: £710 for 7 nights, all-in — cheapest live quote, see full pricing below

That's $931 total including taxes & fees for 13–20 March 2027 (2 guests, 1 double room, breakfast included on that rate). Booking.com quoted £1,151 for the same week — so shop around for this hotel. Full breakdown in the pricing panel below.

Downtown · step up

Giza · pyramid view

Guardian Pyramids Hotel

Budget-friendly rooms a short walk from the Giza plateau entrance — wake up, look out, there they are. Worth it for one or two nights; a long taxi ride from the rest of Cairo.

Consider 1 night here + the rest in Zamalek.

Why Zamalek wins

It's the one part of Cairo where the evening plan is a walk: along the Corniche at sunset, a felucca from the dock below, dinner on a side street — no taxi negotiations required.

The week, day by day

Switch between the two plans — the shape of the week is the same in either month. Both start gently: Cairo rewards early starts and unhurried evenings. In March, 24°C afternoons are made for long lunches; in April, plan the same days with earlier starts in the south. Sample weeks: Saturday 13 – Saturday 20 March, or Saturday 10 – Saturday 17 April 2027.

1Sat

Arrive & settle in

Land at Cairo International, transfer to Zamalek, shake off the flight with a walk along the Nile Corniche. Sunset felucca ride (about an hour, agree the price before you step on), then dinner in Zamalek.

Overnight: Cairo · Easy day

2Sun

The Pyramids & the Grand Egyptian Museum

Early start for the Giza plateau — the Great Pyramid of Khufu, Khafre, Menkaure and the Sphinx — before the heat and the tour buses. Then the Grand Egyptian Museum next door: the colossal Ramses II, the Grand Staircase and the complete Tutankhamun collection in its new home. Book the GEM time slot ahead.

Overnight: Cairo · The big day — go early

3Mon

Saqqara, Dahshur & Memphis

Older than Giza: Djoser's Step Pyramid at Saqqara — the first pyramid ever built — the Bent and Red Pyramids at Dahshur (you can climb inside the Red Pyramid), and the fallen colossus of Ramses II at Memphis. A private driver for the day is the easy way to do this loop.

Overnight: Cairo · Full day, private driver ≈ £40–£60

4Tue

Islamic Cairo — Citadel & the bazaar

The Citadel of Saladin and the alabaster Mosque of Muhammad Ali for the great view over the city, then down into the medieval lanes: Sultan Hassan mosque and the Khan el-Khalili bazaar for lanterns, brass and mint tea at El Fishawy café, trading since 1773.

Overnight: Cairo · Haggle with a smile — start at half

5Wed

Coptic Cairo & the old Egyptian Museum

The Hanging Church, the Ben Ezra Synagogue and the Coptic Museum in the morning; the historic Egyptian Museum on Tahrir Square in the afternoon — still packed with royal statues and treasures even after the GEM opened. Slow evening: dinner cruise or a Zamalek rooftop.

Overnight: Cairo · Gentler pace

6Thu

Day trip — Alexandria or the Fayoum

Alexandria (2½ hrs by train): the Bibliotheca Alexandrina, the Citadel of Qaitbay on the harbour where the Pharos lighthouse stood, and seafood on the Corniche. Or the Fayoum oasis: waterfalls at Wadi El Rayan, pottery villages and flamingos on Lake Qarun. Pick one — not both.

Overnight: Cairo · Alexandria train ≈ £10–£18 return

7Fri–Sat

Slow morning & home

Last look at the bazaar for gifts, coffee in Zamalek, and a final felucca if the light is good. Transfer to the airport for the flight home — aim to be at CAI three hours before departure.

Depart Sat 20 Mar (March) or Sat 17 Apr (April)

1Sat

Arrive & settle in

Land at Cairo International, transfer to Zamalek. Evening stroll on the Corniche, sunset felucca on the Nile, dinner nearby. Early night — tomorrow is the big one.

Overnight: Cairo · Easy day

2Sun

The Pyramids & the Grand Egyptian Museum

Giza plateau first thing — Great Pyramid, Khafre, Menkaure, the Sphinx and the panoramic viewpoint — then the Grand Egyptian Museum: Ramses II in the atrium, the Grand Staircase, and Tutankhamun's treasures complete for the first time. Pre-book the GEM slot.

Overnight: Cairo · Go early, take water

3Mon

Old Cairo, then fly south

Morning in Islamic Cairo — the Citadel and Muhammad Ali Mosque — and a first wander in Khan el-Khalili. Late-afternoon flight Cairo → Aswan (1 hr 20 mins), board your cruise ship and sleep on the Nile. (Cruises Aswan → Luxor typically sail Mon / Wed / Fri — we'll match the flight to the sailing.)

Overnight: On board, Aswan

4Tue

Aswan — Philae & the High Dam

With the ship's Egyptologist: the island Temple of Philae, rescued stone by stone from the rising lake; the Unfinished Obelisk in its granite quarry; and the Aswan High Dam. Afternoon sailing north to Kom Ombo, whose twin temple glows at dusk.

Overnight: On board, sailing · Optional: Abu Simbel day trip

5Wed

Edfu & on to Luxor

Morning at Edfu — the best-preserved temple in Egypt, dedicated to Horus the falcon god — then a lazy afternoon on deck through the Esna lock, arriving in Luxor for an evening visit to Luxor Temple, floodlit and unforgettable.

Overnight: On board, Luxor

6Thu

Valley of the Kings & Karnak, fly back

Disembark after breakfast for Luxor's West Bank: three royal tombs in the Valley of the Kings, Hatshepsut's terraced temple and the Colossi of Memnon; then Karnak's forest of columns on the East Bank. Evening flight Luxor → Cairo (1 hr).

Overnight: Cairo

7Fri–Sat

Buffer day & home

A spare day in Cairo — deliberately. Anything the weather or the khamsin wind disrupted can slot in here; otherwise it's Saqqara, the old Egyptian Museum, or pure bazaar time. Fly home Saturday.

Depart Sat 20 Mar (March) or Sat 17 Apr (April)

The Nile cruise, in detail

What the boat does

The ship is hotel, transport and tour bus in one: it sails the ~210 km between Aswan and Luxor while you sleep, moors beside the temples, and a licensed Egyptologist takes you round each site. Full board is standard; there's a sun deck and usually a small pool.

What it costs (per person) — March vs. April

3 nights, Aswan → Luxor — March (high season): from ≈ $520–$700 standard 5-star · $880–$1,050 deluxe
3 nights, same sailing — April (shoulder): from ≈ $440–$595 standard · $750–$890 deluxe — roughly 15–20% less
4 nights, Luxor → Aswan: from ≈ $590–$820 standard in March · ≈ $500–$700 in April · $1,250+ deluxe

Prices usually include cabin, all meals on board, guided sightseeing and site entrance fees; drinks, tips and the optional Abu Simbel trip (from Aswan, ≈ $90–$120) are extra. This cruise gap is the whole price story between the two months — everything else is much the same. Note the March sample week (ending 20 March) deliberately finishes just before the Easter peak supplement that cruise lines apply from 21 March.

Getting there: fly Cairo → Aswan and back from Luxor (about an hour each way). The overnight sleeper train Cairo–Aswan is the romantic alternative and saves a hotel night.

Don't miss: the Grand Egyptian Museum

Opened in late 2025 beside the Giza plateau, the GEM is now the single biggest reason to come to Cairo — the largest archaeological museum in the world, holding the complete Tutankhamun collection together for the first time. It's in both plans, on Day 2, paired with the Pyramids.

Don't miss: the view from the Citadel

From Saladin's Citadel the whole of Cairo spreads out below the Mosque of Muhammad Ali — on a clear spring morning you can see all the way to the Pyramids. Go before 10am for the clearest air, in either month.

And leave an evening for Khan el-Khalili

Cairo's great bazaar since 1382 — lantern-sellers, spice stalls, brass and glass in medieval lanes off al-Azhar. It's at its best after dark, when the shops light up. Prices are a starting point for a friendly negotiation, not a bill; walk away smiling and the real price usually follows you.

Good to know — for either month

Weather & what to pack

  • March: 24°C by day, 13°C at night in Cairo, ~30°C in Luxor and Aswan. April: 28°C in Cairo, ~35°C in the south — pack the same, but add a stronger hat and plan southern sights early. Both months are warm, dry, almost no rain; evenings are cooler in March, so bring a proper layer for the felucca and cruise deck.
  • The khamsin — a hot, dusty desert wind — can blow on a few days between March and May, though it peaks in April. Sunglasses, a scarf and a spare indoor plan (the GEM is perfect) cover it.
  • Ramadan is expected to run to about 8 March 2027, with Eid al-Fitr around 9 March — the March sample week starts just after, and April is well clear of it, so restaurants, sites and boats are on normal hours for both options.
  • Loose, light clothing that covers shoulders and knees for mosques and churches; a scarf for head-covering where asked.
  • Sun hat, high-factor sunscreen, comfortable closed shoes — temple floors are ancient stone.

Money & getting around

  • Currency is the Egyptian pound (EGP). Cards work in hotels and big shops; carry small cash notes for taxis, tips and the bazaar.
  • Uber and Careem work well in Cairo and end the taxi-price negotiation before it starts.
  • Tipping (baksheesh) is a way of life — small notes for guides, drivers and boat crews; budget a few pounds a day.
  • Site tickets increasingly card-only at the gate; the Giza plateau general ticket was ≈ 700 EGP in 2026.

Book ahead

  • Grand Egyptian Museum timed slot — book as soon as dates are fixed.
  • The Nile cruise sailing that matches the internal flights (Mon / Wed / Fri departures from Aswan).
  • Internal flights Cairo ↔ Aswan / Luxor at the same time as the London flights.
  • E-Visa at least 7 days before departure, and print it.

Eat & drink

  • Koshari — Egypt's national dish of rice, lentils, pasta and crispy onions — at Abou Tarek, Downtown.
  • Ful and ta'ameya (Egyptian falafel, made with fava beans) for breakfast like a Cairene.
  • Mint tea or Turkish coffee at El Fishawy in Khan el-Khalili; fresh sugarcane and mango juice from street stalls.
  • Drink bottled or filtered water; ice in good restaurants is fine.
